rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING GOVERNMENT HOSPITALS TO UTILIZE ALL INCOME FOR THEIR MAINTENANCE AND OTHER OPERATING EXPENSES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The practice of NOT allowing government hospitals to spend their income for maintenance and other operating expenses RESTRICTS their willingness to respond to the needs of their clients and rules out the initiative to expand and improve their services.

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO UPGRADE THE SALARY SCALE OF A RETIRING GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEE BY ONE GRADE FOR PURPOSES OF HIS/HER RETIREMENT
rows.abstract: The salary scale of any retiring government employee shall be upgraded to one grade on the date of his/her retirement. The upgraded salary scale shall be the basis in computing the retirement benefits of such retiring employee. For any employee whoopts to retire under any existing laws on retirement, the one-grade increase shall be deemed granted one year before retirement for purposes of service requirement only.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 1999-04-26

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMOTING AND REGULATING THE OPERATION OF THE USED/WASTE OIL RECYCLING INDUSTRY
rows.abstract: "Oil Recycling Act of 1999". USED/WASTE OIL refers to lubricating oils that have gone through their intended use cycle. This measure proposes that the government take an active role in all facets of used/waste oil recycling, whether as a large-scaleindustry or an ordinary community activity by formulating specific guidelines, providing support services and granting tax incentives.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 1999-04-26

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1638, AS AMENDED BY PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1650, ENTITLED 'ESTABLISHING A NEW SYSTEM OF RETIREMENT AND SEPARATION FOR MILITARY PERSONNEL OF THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES'
rows.abstract: Rationale: The AFP is burdened by an "age-based" rather than "performance-or iented" retirement system.  This system results in a longer length of service of those commissioned in the service at a young age against those commissioned at a later age.This bill proposes a NEW retirement system to correct this situational inconsistency.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE since 1999-04-26

rows.title_full: AN ACT SETTING ASIDE TWENTY-FIVE PERCENT (25%) OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS CALAMITY FUNDS FOR PREPARATORY ACTIVITIES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: This bill provides that TWENTY -FIVE PERCENT (25%) OF THE CALAMITY FUNDS SHALL BE SET ASIDE AND EXCLUSIVELY EXPENDED FOR PREPARATORY ACTIVITIES FOR CALAMITIES OR DISASTERS THAT MAY OCCUR DURING THE BUDGET YEAR WHICH ACTIVITIES SHALL INCLUDE, BUT NOTLIMITED TO DISSEMINATION OF INFORMATION ON WHAT TO DO BEFORE, DURING AND AFTER THE CALAMITY AND FOR LGU'S TO PINPOINT, REINFORCE AND STRENGTHEN RELOCATION CENTERS, PROCUREMENT OF MEDICINES, BLANKETS, FOOD AND OTHER BASIC NECESSITIES AND FOR STEPS TOBE TAKEN TO MINIMIZE, IF NOT PREVENT, LOSS OF LIVES AND DAMAGE TO PROPERTIES.
rows.status: Substituted by HB08456
